concerns.text: The plan substitutes Formation Energy for Elastic Modulus (see FR-001). This proxy does not directly measure the intended construct (elastic modulus), compromising construct validity for any conclusions about UQ performance on elastic‑modulus prediction.

The Wilcoxon signed‑rank test is applied to per‑sample absolute errors or interval widths, but Calibration Error is a distribution‑level metric. Using a per‑sample test for calibration error is statistically inappropriate and may lead to invalid inference.

Test‑set size is capped at ≥100 samples per dataset. No power analysis is provided, and with only 100 paired observations the study may be under‑powered to detect modest but practically important differences between UQ methods.

The plan performs many pairwise Wilcoxon tests (6 pairs × 3 datasets = 18 tests) but explicitly states that no multiple‑comparison correction is required. This inflates the family‑wise Type I error rate, violating the Statistical‑Rigor Standard of the constitution.

Calibration Error and Sharpness are mentioned but not formally defined (e.g., Expected Calibration Error, interval width variance). Ambiguous metric definitions hinder reproducibility and construct validity.

The plan mentions running paired Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests but does not specify which statistical‑result contract (statistics.schema.yaml vs. stats.schema.yaml) the output will conform to, creating ambiguity between two overlapping contracts.

The plan refers to datasets and UQ methods without explicitly naming the corresponding data‑model entities (MaterialsDataset, UQMethod, EvaluationMetric, StatisticalTestResult). This makes it unclear that every step operates on a defined entity, violating the Plan ↔ Data‑Model consistency requirement.
